title: Unconscious Casualty & Recovery Position
summary: Someone unresponsive but breathing normally should be rolled onto their side to keep the airway open. Keep checking their breathing.

callEmergency.headline: Call {EMERGENCY} for anyone who is unresponsive
when: Breathing becomes abnormal or stops – start CPR

steps.title: Check breathing
steps.text: Open the airway and check for normal breathing (up to 10 seconds). If not breathing normally, start CPR.

steps.title: Roll them onto their side
points: Place the arm nearest you at a right angle to the body
Bring the far arm across the chest and hold the back of their hand against the cheek nearest you
Pull on the far knee to roll them towards you onto their side
Tilt the head back slightly to keep the airway open; adjust the hand under the cheek
Adjust the upper leg so hip and knee are at right angles

steps.title: Monitor
steps.text: Check breathing regularly. If they stop breathing normally, roll them onto their back and start CPR.

steps.title: If a spinal injury is suspected
steps.text: Only roll them if you need to keep the airway clear (vomiting, or you must leave them). Keep the head, neck and body in line, with helpers if possible.

warningSigns: Breathing becomes noisy, irregular or stops
doNot: Do not leave them on their back if breathing and unresponsive
Do not give anything by mouth

sources.body: American Heart Association and American Red Cross
sources.title: 2024 American Heart Association and American Red Cross Guidelines for First Aid
International Consensus on CPR and ECC Science With Treatment Recommendations (CoSTR)

review.notes: Drafted from the cited guidelines. Must be checked by a qualified clinician against the current editions and local protocols before operational use.
